quote: Sure. I'd love to hear what the quote would be.
stewart_read: Customer opens with unsolicited eagerness for pricing — a strong buying signal the rep could have leaned into more explicitly.
coaching_implication: Rep could reflect this excitement back ('sounds like you're ready to see real numbers') to build momentum rather than moving straight into rote qualifying questions.

quote: I just got a few questions so we can start on your design.
stewart_read: Rep never asks what interested the customer in solar — the emotional anchor item was skipped entirely per verified events.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest missed anchor on the call; without it the rep has no emotional hook to tie the appointment to later.

stewart_read: Rep appears to say goodbye mid-call by mistake, confusing the customer about whether the call ended.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a diarization artifact (rep talking to someone else, e.g. a manager) rather than a true call-ending line.
coaching_implication: Regardless of cause, the rep should confirm with the customer immediately rather than let 5+ seconds of ambiguity pass before customer asks 'are you leaving?'

quote: We are interested in solar panels for sure. The timing to make it immediately may not be right for us right now
stewart_read: Customer references a prior in-person solar conversation ('I talked to the guy that came on by') and a timing hesitation; rep does not probe which company or what was discussed, just redirects to specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically deferring detailed discovery to the specialist per setter-scope discipline, which is defensible.
coaching_implication: A quick probe ('what did that quote look like?') would have armed the handoff brief with competitive context for the closer.

quote: Yeah. No. You like, my job is to just do what I just did, get you on the schedule, get you a design build.
stewart_read: Rep correctly holds setter scope, redirecting the timing/quote question to the closer instead of over-explaining or debating.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example — reinforce this exact move as the escape-hatch pattern with the rep.

quote: No. No. No. No. This this quote is completely complimentary.
stewart_read: Customer pushes for the quote now; rep reassures on cost but does not flip the bill ($120) into a why-act-now anchor, just neutralizes the objection.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the appointment was already essentially secured and a flip was unnecessary friction.
coaching_implication: Even a light flip ('that $120 will only go up — let's get you real numbers') would reinforce urgency into the booked slot.
